Research progress report · Place195 · V6–V9 · 6 September 2026

Prospective path information from cue-period hippocampal recordings

Methods, results and validity review: from geometry-defined route components to time-resolved PCA and a first GPU CEBRA benchmark.

Purpose: explain the scientific question, the reasoning behind each iteration, and the evidence needed to judge the findings—without assuming familiarity with the analysis code or the cited representation-learning methods.

Interpretation boundary: this is an exploratory, condition-level pseudopopulation study, not a trial-specific H1 demonstration. An early behavioral probe exposed the original holdout; all subsequent reported model evaluation used development validation. No pristine confirmatory test result is claimed.

Prepared for professor discussion. This document presents existing analyses plus deterministic checks of their saved artifacts; it is not a new fitting run. The V5 professor report is a historical presentation reference, not the current validity status.

Question & foundationsPrior knowledgeFindingsDataflowIteration reviewValidityCritique requestedFull results & provenanceEvidence mapReferences

1. Scientific question and foundations

We are not simulating the hippocampus. We observe a small selection of its activity, describe the animal’s later movement, and test a statistical relationship between the two. The hippocampus is a brain region studied for spatial and memory-related activity; that background motivates the question but does not establish the answer in this recording.

The experiment does not directly observe a complete neural population state. A recorded unit is a putative neuron identified by spike-sorting procedures; the supplied measurement is a sequence of spike times. Counting those events gives a feature. Treating a collection of such features as a coherent population state requires additional evidence about simultaneous recording and timing.

FACT · checked

What the pipeline does

It defines a future corridor component from behavior, constructs cue-count features, then compares raw counts, PCA, and CEBRA with a simple classifier.

INFERENCE · bounded

What the results support

This selected, label-conditioned synthetic benchmark did not establish robust whole-cue predictive improvement under its primary evaluation.

UNCHECKED / unresolved

What remains outside the evidence

Authoritative cue/start/goal semantics, simultaneous groups, full selection provenance, nuisance controls, and a genuinely unexposed confirmation dataset.

The central distinction: a pipeline can compute its benchmark correctly without that benchmark answering the original biological question. Software correctness, useful statistical evidence, and biological interpretation are three different gates.

Confidence is high about the inspected transformations and saved scores. It is not high about unverified biological metadata. Code and artifact cross-checks support the computational account; they do not substitute for protocol verification, external peer review, or biological replication.

1.1 The operational objective and solution method

The ideal question is whether cue activity adds information about later path after start and goal are known: I(path; cue activity | start, goal) > 0. This is the conceptual question, not a directly fitted information estimator. A practical test compares an endpoint-only predictor with an endpoint-plus-neural predictor on genuinely held-out real trials.

H1a: information

Does earlier activity help predict later route variation beyond endpoints?

H1b: organization

If that information exists, is its low-dimensional organization reproducible?

These are linked but not interchangeable. Failure of PCA or CEBRA does not prove the absence of information. A beautiful supervised embedding does not prove information beyond the factors that supplied its labels.

What this run actually tests

For D_N_R_T__N_R_M—the directed right-hand upper-to-middle corridor traversal—fix inferred endpoint pair 4→3 and distinguish present from absent. Then ask whether a simple classifier can distinguish synthetic populations assembled from those conditions using separate training and validation sources.

Holding the pair fixed removes variation in operational endpoint identity: an endpoint-only classifier is constant within this task. It does not remove gaze, visual input, heading, history, preparation, or session effects. The IDs themselves are provisional marker-derived meanings, not a verified task protocol.

Competing explanations remain: route-related activity, correlated sensory or preparatory activity, unstable source sampling, or biological information that this selected population/target cannot reveal. A score must discriminate explanations—not merely be larger than another score.

Solution method: first improve the behavioral ruler and support accounting; then retain time; compare linear compression before nonlinear embeddings; finally challenge apparent successes with null analyses that preserve source dependencies. V6 is not a learned brain model. V7/V8 were one predeclared baseline job, separated here to explain their different questions.

2. What was known before the outcomes?

The broad question predates these models: does cue-period activity contain information about a later path beyond start and goal? Earlier place/view/goal analyses and reports of prospective spatial representations motivate the question, but do not establish the result in this dataset. A successful prediction would still need interpretation against sensory, behavioral and history alternatives; it would not establish intention or causal planning.

Knowledge available entering V6 Implication for the next design
195 selected cue-accessible cells across 58 sessions; 1–8 selected units per session. Simultaneous recording groups were not verified. Do not equate the selected-cell union with one 195-dimensional real-trial population. Determine support at the source/session/condition level.
Imported cue-relative events, count windows, source IDs and later Unity paths were available. Task-marker semantics remained provisional. Time binning was technically possible, but correct cue/end-point interpretation remained a metadata condition, not a consequence of array shape.
The maze was a broad 40×40 floor grid with four 8×8 pillar footprints: 1,344 walkable centroids, at 0.625 Unity-coordinate spacing. A grid node’s degree is not a cognitive decision count. Use explicit spatial regions/corridors while retaining raw paths. Do not assume coordinates are meters.
V5 had fragmented route labels and 74.28% masked entries in its older pseudopopulation. Shared components and an observed common panel could improve the measurement problem; more complex neural models would not repair missing support.

The chronology matters

The initial V6 endpoint probe was not split-filtered. Its aggregates exposed held-out behavior and may have influenced design expectations. That worker was stopped before producing accepted graph artifacts; derivation was restarted using static geometry and guarded development inputs. This reset did not undo the exposure. The older V5 report’s statement that the test was untouched describes its earlier stage and is not current.

After accepted geometry/support review, the 29-cell panel and bounded raw/PCA comparisons were fixed. V7/V8 ran together in one predeclared job. The perfect individual-bin result and missing training metrics then prompted V8b diagnostics. The whole-cue input was retained for V9; neither a favorable bin nor a favorable seed replaced the primary specification.

Comparison with V5: the target changed from an older multiclass route/signature problem to a within-endpoint binary component contrast. Accuracy values from those versions are not a common performance trend. The meaningful progression is in measurement, support accounting, temporal features, and evaluation discipline.

Scientific or methodological question Observed result Interpretation
Can routes be represented by reusable, geometry-defined components? A fixed-endpoint present/absent contrast was identified and mapped with complete operational coverage. Behavioral measurement and feasibility improved; cognition was not measured by the graph itself.
Does the whole-cue count pattern generalize in the primary synthetic benchmark? Raw ten-bin mean BA 0.474; PCA-3 0.521 with a 0.258–0.789 seed range; PCA-8 0.453. No stable whole-cue improvement was established. A favorable mean/seed is not sufficient.
Does the perfect 200–300 ms bin provide a convincing timing result? BA 1.0 in three seeds; pointwise source-null p=0.099; max-over-ten-bin p=0.218. The score is reproducible on these synthetic arrays, but not persuasive after the specified selection-aware null.
Does the first CEBRA benchmark improve the result? 12 observed and 40 full-pipeline null fits; predeclared dim8/seed0 p=0.857 for Time and 0.619 for Behavior. The bounded comparison was nonpositive. It does not establish general failure of CEBRA or absence of a biological code.

The defensible conclusion is progress in behavioral measurement and validation design, together with unstable/nonpositive evidence in this particular source-label-conditioned pseudopopulation benchmark—not a demonstration or refutation of trial-specific hippocampal path coding.

Full probability scores, all observed CEBRA runs, the finite null scope and known failed attempts are retained below. Isolated high AUROC and below-chance inversions are discussed rather than hidden.

4. End-to-end dataflow and the evaluation object

Why the gold arrow matters: constructing a synthetic “present” row requires knowing which source trials were later labelled present. If handed a new real trial during its cue, we could not use its unknown future label to fetch matching recordings from other dates. That does not make all condition-level pseudopopulation work meaningless. It makes its question narrower.

The code makes this dependency explicit: scripts/place195_v7_v8_neural_experiments.py:250–305 filters each source pool by its label, copies one whole session block, and builds the two labelled classes separately. That is the assembly seam—not just an incidental implementation name.

5. Iteration-by-iteration methods, results and decisions

V6. A better ruler for movement—not discovery of a neural graph

A centroid says where a tiny floor cell is. A corridor says how larger parts of the maze connect. The maze is a thick two-dimensional floor around pillars, so a floor cell with four neighbors is not necessarily a four-way cognitive decision. Contracting grid paths by node degree alone would confuse floor thickness with meaningful junctions.

The accepted static representation has 9 node/plaza regions, 12 corridors, and 24 directed components. It retains raw coordinates, corridor-axis progress and lateral displacement. Direction is inferred from neighboring regions or progress, with weaker evidence distinguished. A directed traversal differs from occupying the corridor or going the other way.

RESULT It mapped 19,162 eligible development paths, with 481 complete route signatures. The selected component within pair 4→3 had train present/absent support 393/153 and validation 82/32.

MEANING We made a manageable, auditable behavioral contrast. Shared components reduce fragmentation of whole-route labels. They do not automatically supply common neural recordings across the resulting conditions. The full cross-endpoint shared-component neural analysis was not established: candidate overlap in both-label validation sessions was only 0–1.

Why the next step followed: hundreds of eligible paths cannot tell us how many comparable recorded neural observations exist. The support gate had to be evaluated before fitting.

Support refinement. See the reuse in the actual saved population

The available 195 selected cells span 58 sessions, not a verified simultaneous 195-cell recording. Requiring both labels in both splits, with at least three training and one validation source per label, produced the primary 29-cell, seven-session panel. It has 82 training and 22 validation source IDs. These IDs are nested in sessions, not evidence for independent animals or independent simultaneous populations.

A pseudopopulation combines recordings from different trials/sessions under a condition. The safe implementation keeps all cells from a session and all their cue bins together. It preserves the available block relationship; it does not reconstruct unobserved cross-session dependence.

Additional deterministic check of the saved validation manifests:
Present rows have at most 1×1×3×2×1×1×1 = 6 possible source-ID combinations. Absent rows have at most 1×2×1×3×1×2×2 = 24. The saved 64 present rows use only 6 distinct combinations in each seed. The 64 absent rows use 23, 23, and 22 across seeds 0/1/2. These are source-combination counts, not counts of independent trials; distinct neural vectors may be fewer.

Increasing synthetic rows samples that finite empirical construction more thoroughly. It does not add recorded biological evidence. Without source reuse, the primary complete-panel validation ceiling is only one row per label, because the smallest required session pools contain one source.

Formally, the construction samples from a product of session-block empirical distributions, Q(X|y) = ∏s P̂s(Xs|y). Here s is a session, y the known component label, and Xs its whole cell-by-bin block. Independence between selected session blocks is imposed by assembly; their actual simultaneous joint distribution was never observed.

Why the next step followed: this panel is adequate for a clearly labelled feasibility benchmark, not a power guarantee. Use simple, inspectable features before asking a flexible encoder to find structure in it.

V7. Count over time—but distinguish time features from a dynamics model

A spike count is the number of observed events in an interval. A zero is observed silence; a missing entry is no available observation. Those are not interchangeable. Total counts erase ordering: two responses can have equal totals but different early/late activity. Giving each time bin its own feature lets a linear readout weight early and late counts differently.

Finer bins improve temporal resolution but reduce expected events per bin; coarser bins average over differences. A simple counting intuition is expected count = rate × observed duration. This is not a fitted Poisson model or proof of the neurons’ distribution.

RESULT Actual cue duration had median 1.01804 s across 423 loaded source–cell windows. The chosen primary horizon was the first nominal second: 39 spikes outside that horizon were omitted explicitly. Full-window events and counts matched when compared over the same full window. The last bin can have less exposure on a shorter cue.

Mean validation balanced accuracy was 0.453 for total counts and 0.474 for ten-bin counts. Balanced accuracy averages the correct-class rates for present and absent; a constant prediction scores 0.5 here.

MEANING Retaining timing did not reliably resolve this benchmark’s problem. It does not prove timing irrelevant. We ran a time-indexed linear readout, not the richer recurrent or multi-bin sequence-model study originally contemplated.

Why the next step followed: perhaps compression could suppress irrelevant variation and preserve useful shared activity. That motivates PCA without assuming it will succeed.

V8. PCA asks about variance, not automatically about route information

PCA—principal component analysis— finds orthogonal directions along which the supplied training vectors vary most. Think of rotating a cloud of points to align with its long axes. It does not know that a small route-related difference is more scientifically important than a large unrelated firing change.

Per-cell training standardization first adjusts feature scales. PCA then projects each 29-cell bin vector into d coordinates. This is one shared cell-space basis across time, not PCA on one flattened 290-dimensional whole-trial vector.

RESULT PCA-3 validation BA was 0.789 / 0.516 / 0.258 across seeds. PCA-8 was 0.367 / 0.492 / 0.500. More retained variance did not produce better route-component validation. The seed ranges include changes in synthetic assembly; they are not biological replications or confidence intervals.

MEANING One favorable projection/assembly did not establish a stable low-dimensional route representation. Moreover, covariance in this assembled distribution is not the simultaneously measured trial-to-trial covariance of a real population. A mathematically valid PCA does not grant the stronger biological interpretation.

Why the next step followed: an unexpectedly perfect individual bin and missing training metrics demanded diagnosis before attributing anything to a nonlinear embedding.

V8b. Why a perfect bin was not promoted

Bin 2—the nominal 200–300 ms interval—gave BA 1.0 in all three seeds. This happened. The question is what evidential weight it carries, given the tiny fixed source pools and the opportunity to inspect ten bins.

A null analysis constructs results under a specified broken association. Here we shuffle the future-component labels at source-trial level, keep whole cell/bin blocks together, rebuild the synthetic populations, and refit the affected models. Merely shuffling final synthetic rows would not reproduce the label-conditioned construction that generated the result.

Question Equally high null results Finite p
Is this pre-specified bin equally impressive? 9 / 100 (1+9)/101 = 0.099
Would some inspected bin be equally impressive? 21 / 100 (1+21)/101 = 0.218

The latter is the relevant ten-bin selection diagnostic. This p-value is a finite tail-frequency estimate under the chosen shuffling procedure, not a probability that the biological hypothesis is false. Its validity depends on exchangeability—whether labels can be reassigned within the chosen strata under the null. Unmeasured history or nuisance structure can complicate that assumption.

Removing the 20180810 cell block lowered bin-2 mean BA to 0.732; removing 20180912 lowered it to 0.589. Other block removals left it perfect. This localizes sensitivity in the input features. It does not identify causal neurons, prove an artifact’s cause, or amount to successful testing on a new held-out session.

Training diagnostics also exposed overconfidence: raw-total seed 0 had training BA 1.0 and log loss 0.0159, versus validation BA 0.4375 and log loss 2.5237. Constant p=0.5 gives log loss 0.6931. Log loss penalizes confident wrong probabilities; it is not a standalone calibration test.

Why the next step followed: keep the whole cue and the fixed comparator. Do not redefine V9 around a bin selected using validation. The authorized first CEBRA run could still test a bounded representation alternative, not manufacture a discovery.

V9. CEBRA optimizes relationships we specify

In contrastive learning, an anchor is a training vector, a positive is another vector declared related to it, and sampled comparisons provide alternatives. An encoder learns to make designated positives relatively similar. CEBRA’s learning task therefore depends on who is called a positive.

CEBRA-Time

Positive = next cue bin in the same pseudo row. The source components stay fixed. The encoder is not given the component-label context, but the rows were assembled with it.

CEBRA-Behavior

Positive = another training observation with the same component label. Labels deliberately shape the geometry. Training separation is not independent discovery of route structure.

A crucial implementation detail: offset1-model receives one 29-cell bin vector at a time. The temporal sampler decides which vectors to compare; it does not give the network a multi-bin input window. A receptive field is what input the network actually reads. A temporal objective is not the same as a temporal receptive field.

RESULT Native CEBRA 0.6.1 ran on an RTX 2070: 12 observed fits (two objectives × two dimensions × three seeds), plus 40 full-pipeline source-label null fits, all 1,000 updates. Raw/PCA models used CPU. Encoder fitting and downstream transformations used training only.

The predeclared dimension-eight, seed-zero source-null comparisons gave p=0.857 for Time and p=0.619 for Behavior. Each uses only 20 permutations, resolution 1/21. The encoder was refitted for every null because relabelling changes the assembled input distribution—even for Time.

Training evidence: optimization progress is not route-prediction success

The fixed training budget is not an exhaustive test of CEBRA. Equally, a decreasing training curve is not a reason to claim biological structure. The held-out readout and source-aware null address a different question from optimization progress.

MEANING This bounded CEBRA comparison did not turn the benchmark into robust prospective-path evidence. It does not show that CEBRA generally fails or that biological information is absent.

Secondary-metric qualification: BA 0.5 alongside AUROC 0.946

CEBRA-Time-3, seed 1, ranked positive validation rows relatively above negative rows: AUROC was 0.946289. But it classified every row as negative at its fitted threshold, so BA was 0.5. AUROC measures ranking across thresholds, not correctness of the fixed decision rule. The other two seeds’ AUROCs were 0.022217 and 0.0.

This is why “poor BA” is not literally “zero information in every score.” It is also why selecting this one secondary score, or retuning the threshold using validation, would not establish a robust primary result. The predeclared null evaluated BA, not an unrestricted search across metrics and seeds. Two complete BA=0 inversions were also checked against saved labels; the earlier audit did not find a label-swap or reshape explanation.

Engineering result, separately: replacing a slow CUDA-index expansion loop with the audited pointwise path reduced one fit from 102.01 to 7.08 seconds. Its 1,000 losses and validation embeddings matched exactly. That is a 14.4× implementation speedup, not a neural-accuracy improvement. The final 52-fit run took about 364 seconds; this excludes earlier attempts and the rest of the project.

Overall: behavioral measurement became more defensible; source accounting became much clearer; whole-cue condition-level evidence remained unstable/nonpositive. Not established is not false. None of these outcomes demonstrates intention, causal planning, or absence of a hippocampal prospective code.

6. Validity assessment, assumptions and failure modes

Reconcile the intended contract with the executed experiment

What the documents say What code / history actually supports Review judgment
The scientific contract requires cue activity and later path on the same real trial, with verified simultaneous population measurements. The implementation deliberately builds labelled cross-session pseudo rows. This is a narrower exploratory question, not completion of the trial-specific H1 gate. Authorization to run CEBRA did not remove the contract’s biological limit.
The intended protocol reserves an untouched test. An early unfiltered endpoint probe breached the holdout contract; accepted work subsequently used guarded development data. Use the incident record, not the nicer pristine-holdout story. New random splits cannot undo inspection of the same data.
The report describes source shuffling within session, split, and endpoint pair. The actual function groups only by split and session; its caller first restricts every source to one endpoint pair. Equivalent here because the endpoint is constant. Unsafe to generalize unchanged to multi-pair pooling. The precondition needs to remain explicit.
“Time-based modeling” could mean a sequence model. Binned linear features and a pointwise CEBRA encoder with temporal positive sampling were executed. Do not describe a recurrent model or verified joint dynamics as completed work.

Invalid inferential shortcuts and their smallest safeguards

The following shortcuts were not adopted in the accepted V6–V9 benchmark. Introducing them would invalidate the corresponding interpretation; the consequences and repairs are stated explicitly.

Treating resampled pseudo rows as independent validation trials understates uncertainty. Consequence: a narrow-looking interval can reflect repeated source blocks, not biological replication. Smallest fix: count source trials/session dependencies and use a justified source-level evaluation or null. Safe defer condition: only label an interval as Monte Carlo error for the synthetic assembly, never as biological confidence.
Filling unavailable cells with zero invents observed silence. Consequence: the classifier can learn recording availability or a fabricated activity pattern. Smallest fix here: restrict to an observed panel and preserve masks until valid block assembly. This rejected shortcut cannot be deferred while making neuronal-response claims.
Selecting the best validation time window and reusing the same validation as confirmation lets evaluation choose the target. Consequence: impressive scores acquire selection bias. Smallest fix: retain the predeclared window, disclose the diagnostic, reproduce the specified selection under an appropriate null, and reserve genuinely unexposed data for confirmation. Exploratory inspection is permissible only when labelled as such.

DESIGN JUDGMENT Pseudopopulation analysis itself is not automatically bad design. It becomes bad design when its condition-level product distribution is sold as a measured single-trial population or deployable unknown-label prediction. Under explicit restrictions, it is a useful feasibility instrument.

Assumptions to inspect—not wish away with passing tests

Must be true / known How to verify next Risk if wrong
Markers really identify cue, start, goal and navigation as interpreted. unchecked metadata Authoritative protocol and example event alignment, not filenames alone. A fixed marker pair need not fix the intended physical/task variables.
Claimed units belong to verified simultaneous recording groups. unresolved Recording-group, acquisition and sorting provenance. Population covariance/state/dynamics interpretation is unsupported.
Conditional permutation strata preserve the required nuisance structure. assumption Review history, time blocks, gaze and other covariates; justify exchangeability. Null frequencies need not be calibrated for the stronger scientific question.
Unknown behavior is not labelled absent; unavailable neural observations are not zero. Inspect mapping/mask guards and representative excluded cases. Manufactured negative labels or fabricated silence drive the model.
Bin edges, partial exposure and clock units match the intended estimand. Check every nominal boundary against acquisition-clock conventions; current focused fixture checks 0.1 s and the one-second horizon, not every possible decimal edge. Subtle timing claims can depend on numerical boundaries or exposure differences. This review did not diagnose an effect on historical spike assignments.
New code using multiple endpoints retains endpoint-specific null strata. Before extension, include endpoint in metadata/shuffle groups or assert single-pair input. The present implicit single-pair protection silently disappears.
Independent validation means independent evidence, not new random seeds. Audit source manifests, session nesting and genuinely unexposed evaluation units. Synthetic replication or adaptive validation is mistaken for confirmation.

Review next: one high-leverage decision

Before approving a larger architecture, ask for a prefit design in which each feature row can be built from one real trial without knowing its future label, with recording groups, endpoints and clocks verified. Then check sufficient within-endpoint route variation, source-aware nuisance baselines, and genuinely unexposed evaluation. That is a change in evidential support; another thousand synthetic draws is not.

If the existing recordings cannot supply that design, retain the explicit condition-level question rather than pretending that preprocessing repaired observability. Better-supported development analyses may still be useful; they do not become pristine confirmation by reshuffling the existing data.

7. Specific critique requested from the professor

The main decisions are about observability and evaluation, rather than another architecture search. The following questions identify what would change the scientific status of the work.

  1. Confirm task semantics. Does the current minor marker identify the goal/cue as assumed, and does the previous successful goal identify the next start? Which cue and navigation events should define the neural window? Is any cue-identity variation left within an endpoint pair?
  2. Confirm recording groups and selection. Which units were acquired simultaneously, how were units curated, and how was the 195-cell cohort selected? Can a real-trial feature matrix be obtained without conditioning its construction on the future label?
  3. Critique the behavioral ruler. Are the proposed junction/plaza and corridor regions appropriate for this task? Which reversals, within-plaza choices or path distinctions must be retained before defining the next operational target?
  4. Choose the next estimand and independent unit. Should the next gate be a within-session real-source baseline, a condition-mean analysis, or a jointly endpoint-controlled shared-component comparison? Specify the minimum route-variant support and source/session-held-out scheme before model fitting.
  5. Identify controls and genuinely unexposed evaluation. Which gaze, view, heading, action, history and clock-quality variables are available? Can new/unexposed observations be reserved before the next adaptive choices? Resplitting inspected observations cannot restore pristine confirmation.
Proposed next gate: verify a dataset/design in which each feature row can be constructed from one real trial before its future label is known; establish adequate controlled route variation; then test a simple source-aware baseline with appropriate nuisance controls and an unexposed confirmation plan. Additional development work on existing data may be useful but should remain labelled as such.

Discussion question: What additional observation would materially strengthen the H1a claim, compared with increasing the number of synthetic draws from the same 22 validation source trials?

8.2 Preprocessing and training specification

Item Accepted specification / scope
Behavior contrast Directed middle component D_N_R_T__N_R_M, within provisional endpoint pair 4→3. Geometry/support choices made without neural predictive-performance selection.
Neural panel and source unit 29 cells / 7 sessions; 82 training and 22 validation source IDs. Source storage 104×29×10 is masked, not 104 simultaneous 29-cell trials.
Assembly 64 rows/class/split, seeds 0/1/2. One source per session block, same source across its cells and cue bins. No missing-value-as-zero imputation.
Time Nominal first second; ten 100 ms bins primary, 50/200 ms sensitivities. Exposure stored. Variable full-cue duration was not silently treated as exactly one second.
PCA Training-only scaler/PCA on 1,280×29 bin vectors; dimensions 3/8 reused across time; whole-cue readout has 30/80 features. Derived vectors remain dependent.
CEBRA Native offset1-model, hidden width 32, output dimensions 3/8, batch 256, 1,000 updates, Adam learning rate 3e-4, fixed cosine temperature 1.0. Time uses same-pseudorow +1-bin positives; Behavior uses same-label positives.
Decoder Logistic regression C=1 with training-only standardization. C=0.1/0.01 were V8b sensitivities, not validation-selected replacements.
V8b null 100 source-label permutations with reassembly/refitting; mean over seeds and max-over-ten-bin statistics matched to the inspected family. Not a correction for every adaptive study choice.
V9 null 20 per variant, dimension eight / seed zero only; source-label permutation, reassembly, scaler/encoder/decoder refit, same 1,000-update budget.
Hardware / software V6 and raw/PCA CPU work; native CEBRA on RTX 2070. Python 3.13.2, NumPy 2.3.4, sklearn 1.7.2, CEBRA 0.6.1, torch 2.12.0+cu130; driver 580.173.02. No environment changes for this document.

10. Method context and reading references

The explanations above stand on their own. The following sources motivate the choice of measurements and models; they do not transfer their biological conclusions to the Place195 benchmark.

  • Johnson & Redish (2007). Prospective spatial representations in rat CA3 during decisions motivate asking whether activity relates to locations beyond the animal’s current position. Task, timing and recording differences prevent assuming the same phenomenon here. doi:10.1523/JNEUROSCI.3761-07.2007.
  • Cunningham & Yu (2014). Dimensionality reduction organizes shared variation in neural populations. The relevant distinction here is explained variance versus task-specific information, and synthetic versus simultaneously measured covariance. doi:10.1038/nn.3776.
  • Schneider et al. (2023), CEBRA. Contrastive learning uses temporal or behavioral relationships to organize embeddings. A chosen positive-pair rule shapes the learned representation; held-out readout remains necessary. doi:10.1038/s41586-023-06031-6.
  • Kobak et al. (2016). Demixed population analyses provide context for separating task-related factors. Demixed PCA was not fitted in this run. doi:10.7554/eLife.10989.
  • Loren Frank Lab track_linearization. A graph-linked spatial ruler and progress variable are useful precedents. A narrow-track HMM mapper was not adopted wholesale for the broad floor. Repository and method documentation.

The primary-paper scope was verified during the research/planning work and documented in its notes. This presentation does not claim a new exhaustive literature review or proof of every CEBRA theoretical assumption.
